question: The conclusion behind U006 was weakened by contradicting work; how should the direction change?
description: The inference-time null does not straightforwardly replicate under fine-tuning. arxiv:2609.12230 fine-tunes Qwen3-14B under exactly the contested contrast (KG-grounded: target triple/path only; CG-grounded: target plus same-source-chunk supporting triples) with matched base model, LoRA setup, optimizer, sequence length, batch size, epochs, learning-rate schedule and equal QA-item counts, and reports that the context-augmented model beats the KG-only model in every disease, evaluation setting and hop length, by 1.98/2.20/2.15 points on Gastroparesis 3/4/5-hop and 1.50-2.66 points for Diabetes. So training does appear to extract value that prompting did not, and the 'premise is false' inference is weakened. What remains open is attribution: the two regimes have equal example counts but the CG examples contain more context tokens, and no token-matched random-distractor control was run, so the gain could still be partly a context-volume or question-distribution effect rather than passage coherence.
rationale: Evidence contradicts the current direction; refine it instead of forcing the evidence to fit.
